title: +PSYCHOLOGY OF DISABILITY
description: Examines disability from social psychological and disability studies perspectives. Emphasizes the social construction of disability and its inter- and intra-personal ramifications. Explores stereotyping, prejudice and discrimination, adaptation to disability, disability identity, working with people with disabilities, intersectionality, and sexuality.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: PSY 201, 201H, 201Z, 201HZ, 202, 202H, 202Z or 202HZ.
A minimum grade of C- is required in PSY 201, PSY 201H, PSY 201Z, PSY 201HZ, PSY 202, PSY 202H, PSY 202Z and PSY 202HZ.

Students with a term class standing of Freshman or Sophomore may not enroll.
recommendations: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course
attribute_description: Core Education - Difference, Power, & Oppression: Advanced (CSDP)
books_html: No-cost: Course utilizes open educational resources, materials available through the library, or does not require any purchased materials.
meeting_html: TR 10am-11:50am in WGND 132 - Wiegand Hall 132 (GP) (9/23 to 12/4)
